statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-84218 (GHSA-c9ff-59g8-m36q) is in Jolokia's JSR-160 proxy (org.jolokia:jolokia-service-jsr160): the default denylist for client-supplied target JMX service URLs only rejected service:jmx:rmi:///jndi/ldap:.*, so ldaps:// and other LDAP URL forms could still make the agent perform a JNDI lookup against an attacker-chosen server (https://github.com/jolokia/jolokia/issues/1049, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c9ff-59g8-m36q). Upstream fixed it in Jolokia 2.6.2 by rejecting every target URL that is not on the configured allowlist: commit https://github.com/jolokia/jolokia/commit/6ef036d78c3b40602f5e32352e97aed7c0fd5241, contained in the v2.6.2 tag (https://github.com/jolokia/jolokia/releases/tag/v2.6.2). Unpacked all 23 published activemq-artemis packages in the DHI Debian repository, 2.55.0-0 through the current 2.57.0-8, for amd64 and arm64 (2.57.0-0 was published for arm64 only; no debug-symbol packages are published for this source), checked each against the repository index SHA-256, and searched every jar and war inside them, recursively, for the jolokia-service-jsr160 classes. Packages 2.55.0-0 through 2.57.0-3 carry jolokia-service-jsr160 2.4.3, inside the web console (web/console.war/WEB-INF/lib), and are affected. From 2.57.0-4 onward every package carries jolokia-service-jsr160 2.6.3, both in /usr/share/activemq-artemis/lib and in the web console, and no other copy of those classes. Disassembling Jsr160RequestHandler confirms the difference: in 2.4.3 a target URL is accepted when no allowlist is set and it does not match the denylist, while in 2.6.3 the handler keeps only an allowlist and returns no connection for any URL that is not on it, which is the upstream fix. 2.57.0-4 is the first fixed package.
